title: Uptime mosaic: staffing & SLO constitution (draft)
content:
Purpose
This doc captures a pragmatic cross-functional plan to staff, govern, and operationalize a small set of high-value SLOs across product, serving-runtime, and platform teams. It's exploratory: a proposed "SLO constitution" (principles + minimal rules), a staffing mosaic (who does what and when), and a short cadence for validation experiments over a 12-week runway.

Context and problem statement
- We have plenty of service-level metrics but inconsistent ownership of SLOs: multiple teams measure latency/cost/availability differently and there is no lightweight governance for emergency tradeoffs.
- Product launches, model rollouts, and Dedicated capacity deployments create cross-team dependencies that produce firefighting rather than proactive capacity planning.

Primary goals (measurable)
1) Establish 3 cross-cutting SLOs (latency p95, token-generation availability, and topology-aware error-rate) with agreed measurement definitions across teams within 6 weeks.
2) Create a staffing mosaic so each SLO has a primary steward + two rotating partners (platform, serving-runtime, product) and an oncall escalation ladder.
3) Run two 30-day validation experiments to compare error-budget-driven rollout vs current ad-hoc rollout behavior; measure change in incident frequency and time-to-rollback.

Scope
- In-scope: API-facing hosted inference, Dedicated ingestion paths, and the internal model deployment pipelines that affect user-facing latency.
- Out-of-scope: peripheral infra (CI/CD for non-ML infra), and low-traffic internal admin endpoints.

SLO constitution: principles + minimal rules
Principles (short and actionable):
- Keep SLOs small in number and high in signal: prefer 2–4 cross-team SLOs, each tied to clear customer impact.
- Single source of truth for measurement: define a canonical pipeline (telemetry + cardinality) stored in the observability project.
- Fast triage: error budget burn should produce an automatic lightweight play (scale, rollout pause, or prioritized bug fix).
- Express tradeoffs: every SLO has an associated cost-sensitivity note (what to do when fixes are expensive).
Minimal rules (constitution clauses):
1) Any proposed SLO must include: definition, owner, measurement pipeline, and a suggested error-budget policy.
2) Owners must publish a 90-day impact ledger (what product lines depend on this SLO).
3) A cross-team SLO council meets weekly during pilot and then biweekly; decisions recorded as short RFCs.

Staffing mosaic (roles & first-12-week rotations)
- Primary steward (week 0–12): Platform-engineering lead (Ava Martinez) — shepherd constitution, telemetry collection, governance.
- Serving-runtime partner: Daniel Kim — responsible for kernel-level regressions affecting p95 and token availability.
- Product partner: Priya Nair — advises on customer impact and rollback priorities.
- Oncall escalation ladder: feature team oncall -> serving-runtime -> platform mobilization -> SRE executive contact.
- Rotation plan: two-week rotations for partners, 12-week steward tenure for continuity.

Key milestones (12-week runway)
- Week 0–2: finalize SLO definitions, instrumentation checklist, and measurement queries (baseline run).
- Week 3–4: implement canonical telemetry pipelines (metrics + trace tags).
- Week 5–6: dry-run error-budget alarms and playbooks in staging (no public impact).
- Week 7–10: run experiment A (error-budget gating for model rollouts); collect signals.
- Week 11–12: run experiment B (automated fallback routing + capacity bump policy); synthesis and decision.

Experiment design (two short experiments)
Experiment A: Error-budget gating for rollouts
- Trigger: model rollout begins -> gate checks error budget at steady-state windows (15m/1h).
- Response: if burn > threshold, pause rollout + notify product + rollback suggestion.
- Outcome measures: proportion of rollouts paused, time-to-detect, customer-facing incidents.

Experiment B: Topology-aware fallback routing
- Trigger: capacity stress/latency spike in primary region -> route traffic to secondary (cost-tiered) model variant.
- Response: automated routing + cache priming + alert to stewards.
- Outcome measures: user error surface area, average latency, cost delta.

Telemetry and observability checklist
- Define canonical metric names and tags (customer_id, model_variant, route_id, region).
- Tracing: ensure token-gen traces include model compile/kv-cache hits and quantization path tags.
- Dashboards: one SLO scoreboard (live error budget view) and a rollouts page with current active experiments.
- Alerting: two alert tiers — soft (dashboard + slack) and hard (pager duty) with explicit silence windows during planned experiments.

Decision heuristics and escalation playbook (short)
- Soft burn (<30% of budget/week): log, owner awareness, no action.
- Moderate burn (30–70%): owner must open a mitigation ticket and limit non-essential rollouts.
- Severe burn (>70%): auto-suspend new rollouts, trigger platform mobilization call.

Risks and mitigations
- Measurement drift risk: mitigate with weekly sample replays and comparison to event logs.
- Over-control (too many rollbacks): start conservative; tune thresholds after first experiment to avoid unnecessary rollbacks.
- Staffing fatigue: keep rotations short, automate routine checks, and document playbooks as runbooks.

Open questions (for council)
- Should error budgets be normalized per-customer tier or global-first approach?
- What is the acceptable cost delta for the fallback routing experiment? (Suggested: cap at +15% token cost per experiment.)
- How do we tie SLOs to commercial SLAs for Dedicated customers? (Legal/compliance input needed.)

Immediate next steps (owners & deadlines)
- By 2026-10-15: finalize and publish SLO definitions to the confluence landing (owner: Ava).
- By 2026-10-22: implement baseline metrics queries and create the scoreboard (owner: Daniel).
- By 2026-10-29: staging alarm dry-run and playbook rehearsal (owner: Priya + serving-runtime).

Notes to self / friction points
- Expect friction with model teams when an automated pause blocks a rollout; build a clear fast-appeal process.
- Keep the initial SLO set intentionally limited to avoid governance paralysis.

Appendix: quick measurement templates (example queries)
- Latency p95: SELECT percentile(lat_ms,95) BY model_variant,route_id,region WHERE status = 200
- Token availability: count(token_generated_successful) / count(token_generation_attempts)

Contact
- Lead: Ava Martinez (ava@redwood.ai) — ping in #platform-uptime with subject [SLO-CONST].

End of draft
